This is a CPU simulation, not a real quantum computer.
A 5.2 μs laser pulse is not the full algorithm runtime. Real QPU wall time was not measured.

What exactly was timed?

Same cities, demands, vehicle count, and capacity. Different guarantees: classical returns the proven optimum; the quantum-assisted heuristic may return a longer route. Classical timing includes exact subset tours and exact partition optimization. Quantum timing includes layout fitting, full state-vector simulation, sampling, validation, and classical trivial/size-fallback routing. No cached exact reference supplies the quantum solution.

These three runs use the same fixed solver seed. They measure timing variability for this workload, not solution variability or a general scaling advantage. File export, module imports, offline scoring, network queues, and real hardware are outside the timer.
